userStories.title: Test-hook keys stop being approvable
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the two production-unreachable fleet test-hook keys non-approvable and open the incremental rollout contract.

**Motivation** — 5a to 5c-2 gated 81 routes.

**Approach** — **The test-hook keys are non-approvable by name.** `catalog.ts` gains `TEST_HOOK_KEYS = new Set(['testhook.schedule.fire', 'testhook.nax-files.seed'])` (exported). `buildEntry` answers `approvable: false` (floor and default `none`) for a member. Its risk stays `medium`, because the rule is about reachability, not risk. No role changes. A policy naming one of these keys is refused by policy validation from then on, as for any non-approvable key.

**Each gating story removes its own `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` rows.** US-001 relaxes the exact gated-route count to a lower bound (at least 81), and the allowlist count case to the `gate-secret` count. US-009 restores both exactly.

US-001: the rows of `POST /fleet/test-hooks/schedules/:id/fire` and `PUT /fleet/test-hooks/repos/:repoId/nax-files` are deleted (their keys are no longer approvable, so the contract would report them stale).

Update `catalog.spec.ts` — the "derives … for every catalog key" case's local approvable rule also excludes TEST_HOOK_KEYS members (import TEST_HOOK_KEYS), so its derivation matches the catalog. In `src/permissions/test-helpers/permission-contract.spec.ts`, the "AC-3: keeps exactly 36 fleet and 11 secret rollout assignments" case asserts only the gate-secret count (11), until US-009. In `test/integration/permissions/permission-contract.integration.spec.ts`, the "collects exactly 81 gated routes" case becomes "at least 81" (its title follows); US-009 restores an exact count. Consumers `approvableKeys()` and `validateApprovalPolicy` should derive their new behavior through catalog approvability.

**Scope** — In: catalog derivation, the two hook allowlist removals and temporary contract assertion relaxation. Out: gating the 16 production routes (US-002–US-008), exact final counts/OpenAPI (US-009), changing hook reachability or role grants. Changing any catalog default: these keys stay `none`. Updating `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv`: the test-hook rule is code (`TEST_HOOK_KEYS`), not an inventory column.

**Interface** — `TEST_HOOK_KEYS = new Set(['testhook.schedule.fire', 'testhook.nax-files.seed'])` (exported); `buildEntry` answers `approvable: false` (floor and default `none`) for a member.

AC-2 [unit]: findCatalogEntry('testhook.schedule.fire')?.risk returns 'medium', unchanged.
AC-3 [unit]: approvableKeys() contains neither testhook.schedule.fire nor testhook.nax-files.seed.
AC-4 [unit]: findCatalogEntry('fleet.ingest.backfill')?.approval.approvable remains true.
AC-5 [unit]: PENDING_GATE_ROUTES.has(route) returns false for each of POST /fleet/test-hooks/schedules/:id/fire and PUT /fleet/test-hooks/repos/:repoId/nax-files (one it.each row each).

userStories.title: Gated job dispatch and requeue, and the ticket auto-start after commit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route job dispatch/requeue through REST commands and move RUN ticket auto-start beyond the owning approval commit.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes still bypass the engine on REST: a policy `fleet.job.dispatch → agent` makes the assistant's `koda_dispatch_job` wait, while the same agent calling `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` dispatches at once.

**Approach** — **The dispatch's ticket auto-start runs after commit.** `FleetJobTicketEffects.onRunDispatched` starts each linked ticket and logs a failure instead of throwing ("C9 D452, after commit"). Inside the execution transaction, a swallowed failure poisons the transaction, and a start inside it is no longer after commit. The method now hands its start loop to `AfterCommitService.defer(task)`, and runs it at once when `defer` answers false (no scope: the immediate path). The approval execution opens the scope, so a deferred dispatch starts its tickets after its commit. This also covers the assistant's `koda_dispatch_job`, whose approved run already dispatches inside the execution transaction.

**A deferred job create that loses the active-job race fails the request.** `FleetJobsService.dispatch`, `.requeue` and `ConfigJobsService.create` catch `DuplicateActiveJobError`, then look up the winner "outside the failed transaction". Inside the execution transaction, that lookup runs in the aborted transaction, and the request settles `failed`. That is the right outcome; the 409 body's `activeJobId` is not reproduced (Out of Scope). 5b's drift check already behaves this way.

**The frozen input is ids, slugs and the validated body.** Project-scoped inputs carry `slug`, so the execution locks the slug to the request's project (`lockProjectSlug`). Ingest inputs are global and carry only the job id.

Register exactly these project-scoped commands in new `fleet/jobs/fleet-job-route.commands.ts`:
- `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` | `fleet.job.dispatch` | `rest:fleet-jobs.dispatch` | `{ slug, projectId, dispatch: parseBody(DispatchFleetJobDto, …) }` | `jobs.dispatch(principal.id, projectId, dispatch, { ticketActor: { principal, projectSlug: slug } })`.
- `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id/requeue` | `fleet.job.requeue` | `rest:fleet-jobs.requeue` | `{ slug, projectId, id }` | `jobs.requeue(principal.id, projectId, id)`.

Id and string members are read with `parseRouteInput`; a body member with `parseBody` of the route's DTO (a missing body member is parsed as `{}`). Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result`. `FleetJobsModule` imports `ApprovalEngineModule`, `AuthRepositoryModule`; provides `FleetJobRouteCommands`. `FleetJobsController` gains `ApprovalRouteGate` last, and only dispatch/requeue change in this story. Each gated handler gains `@ApprovalGated()`, keeps its `@Requires`, `@HttpCode` and `@ApiResponse`s. On pending throw `new ApprovalPending(outcome.request)`; on executed answer `JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result)` with today's 201/200. **Only the HTTP handlers change.** Gated handlers keep their parameters, in order. This preserves the existing HTTP handler signatures and parameter order; it does not exclude the explicitly scoped commands, module wiring or ticket-effects changes above.

Remove only the dispatch and requeue rows from `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES`. `FleetJobTicketEffects` constructor gains `AfterCommitService` last. Every construction in `fleet-job-ticket.effects.spec.ts` (lines 20, 57 and 185) passes `new AfterCommitService()` as the 6th argument; existing start assertions still hold (no scope is open there); add deferred-start cases. `bundle-ingest.workflow.spec.ts`'s construction also passes `new AfterCommitService()` as the 6th argument; no assertion changes.

Test fixtures: agent holds fleet.job.dispatch and fleet.job.requeue in P. Seed each wait policy explicitly; these keys default to none. Dispatch body is `{ repoId: world.repoId, command: 'RUN', feature: <unique>, maxCostUsd: 5 }`; use independent CREATED tickets and jobs for each criterion.

**Scope** — In: dispatch/requeue gate, commands/module, shared ticket-start timing and affected constructions. Out: cancel and unlink (US-003), config job prepare (US-005), final contracts/OpenAPI (US-009). Assistant or MCP writes on these keys: they keep their primary command. Reproducing the `activeJobId` of the 409 `fleet.jobs` / `fleet.configJobActive` body on a deferred job create that loses the active-job race: the request settles `failed` (Design). The activity rows of the ingest and job writes still record `actorType: 'USER'` for an agent actor, as today. A transaction timeout other than Prisma's default for the execution transaction: a deferred dispatch's placement and a deferred backfill run inside it as they are. Bounding the size of a frozen input: `DispatchFleetJobDto`, `SubmitConfigEditDto.edits` and the patterns list are stored whole in `ApprovalRequest.input` when a request waits. US-002 only: retrying a ticket auto-start that failed after commit; it is logged, as today.

**Interface** — `FleetJobRouteCommands`, `FLEET_JOB_ROUTE_VARIANTS` — new: `dispatch`, `requeue`; `FleetJobsService.dispatch(actorId, projectId, dto, opts)`, `.requeue(actorId, projectId, jobId)`; `FleetJobTicketEffects.onRunDispatched`; `AfterCommitService.defer(task)` answers false outside a scope.

userStories.title: Gated job cancel and ticket-job unlink
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate cancel and unlink while preserving requester cancellation without a cancel key and rechecking authority when execution occurs.

**Motivation** — The fleet writes still bypass the engine on REST: a policy `fleet.job.dispatch → agent` makes the assistant's `koda_dispatch_job` wait, while the same agent calling `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` dispatches at once.

**Approach** — **Cancel keeps "a requester may cancel its own job".** `fleet.job.cancel` is not ownable: the route declares it `enforcedBy: 'service'`, and `FleetJobsService.cancel` lets the requester through without it. The handler first asks `FleetJobsService.requesterOf(projectId, id)` (new), for every caller. That method throws `NotFoundAppException({}, 'fleet.jobs')` for a job missing from the project, as today's 404. The handler then asks `permissions.can(principal, 'fleet.job.cancel', { projectId })`. When that is denied and the requester is not the caller, it throws `ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions')`, as today's 403. It then gates with `keyCheck: false`, because a requester holds no key to check. The command computes `canOperate` again at execution, as 5b's schedule delete computes `canAdminister`, and `FleetJobsService.cancel` re-checks requester-or-key. The engine's execution pre-check (`ApprovalExecutionService.precheck`) re-checks the actor's key for every command, not only prepared ones, so a requester without the key would settle `permission-revoked`. The cancel command therefore sets `skipKeyRecheck: true`: its run is its own authority, as 5a's decide is.

Extend `FleetJobRouteCommands` and its spec (both created by US-002) with cancel registration and run cases. Add `TicketFleetJobRouteCommands` and its spec. Project-scoped route contracts:
- `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id/cancel` | `fleet.job.cancel` | project, `keyCheck: false` | `rest:fleet-jobs.cancel` | `{ slug, projectId, id }` | `jobs.cancel(principal.id, projectId, id, <can fleet.job.cancel at execution>)`; `skipKeyRecheck: true`.
- `DELETE /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/fleet-jobs/:jobId` | `fleet.ticket-job.unlink` | project | `rest:ticket-fleet-jobs.unlink` | `{ slug, projectId, ref, jobId }` | `fleetTickets.unlink(projectId, ref, jobId, principal.id)`, answering `null`.

Id and string members are read with `parseRouteInput`. The cancel command declares `toResult: (result) => result`; the no-body unlink command declares none. `FleetTicketsModule` imports `ApprovalEngineModule`, `AuthRepositoryModule`; provides `TicketFleetJobRouteCommands`. `TicketFleetJobsController` gains `ApprovalRouteGate` last; unlink is gated. Keep existing handler parameters in order, guards, @Requires, @HttpCode and response decorators; add @ApprovalGated. Pending throws ApprovalPending; executed cancel returns JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result), executed unlink has no body/204. Remove exactly the cancel and unlink rows from PENDING_GATE_ROUTES. Existing dispatch/requeue behavior belongs to US-002 and stays intact.

The keyed agent holds fleet.job.cancel and fleet.ticket-job.unlink in P. The requester agent holds fleet.job.dispatch in P and no fleet.job.cancel. Each cancel test inserts its own QUEUED job. A linked job is dispatched by root with `{ repoId: world.repoId, command: 'RUN', feature: <unique>, maxCostUsd: 5, ticketRefs: [<a ticket of P>] }`. Each test repeats its own pending call before approval; do not share another test's request.

**Scope** — In: requesterOf, pre-gate checks, cancel command extension, unlink command/module/controller and their two allowlist removals. Out: changing dispatch/requeue or ticket-start timing (US-002), schedule authority (US-004), final exact contract/export (US-009).

**Interface** — `FleetJobsService.requesterOf(projectId, jobId)` — new: the job's `requestedById`; 404 `fleet.jobs` when missing from the project. `FleetJobsService.cancel(actorId, projectId, jobId, canOperate)`. `TicketFleetJobRouteCommands`, `TICKET_FLEET_JOB_ROUTE_VARIANTS` — new: `unlink`. `FleetTicketsService.unlink(projectId, ref, jobId, actorId)`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration]: POST /api/projects/web/fleet/jobs/<job>/cancel by the keyed agent under a wait policy answers 202 with data matching { permissionKey: 'fleet.job.cancel', projectId: <P's id> }.
AC-2 [integration]: Approving the keyed agent's own AC-1-equivalent request leaves the job CANCELLED, and the request's result.state is CANCELLED.
AC-3 [integration]: POST /api/projects/web/fleet/jobs/<job>/cancel by the requester agent on a job it requested, under a wait policy, answers 202 with data.permissionKey 'fleet.job.cancel'.
AC-4 [integration]: Approving the requester agent's own AC-3-equivalent request leaves the job CANCELLED.
AC-5 [integration]: POST /api/projects/web/fleet/jobs/<job>/cancel by the requester agent on a job dev requested answers 403 with key permissions and writes no ApprovalRequest row.
AC-6 [integration]: POST /api/projects/web/fleet/jobs/<unknown id>/cancel by the keyed agent under a wait policy answers 404 with key fleet.jobs and writes no ApprovalRequest row.
AC-7 [integration]: Approving the keyed agent's pending cancel after root cancelled the same job while it waited settles the request failed.
AC-8 [integration]: DELETE /api/projects/web/tickets/<ref>/fleet-jobs/<job> on a linked job by the keyed agent under a wait policy answers 202 with data.permissionKey 'fleet.ticket-job.unlink'.
AC-9 [integration]: Approving the keyed agent's own AC-8-equivalent request removes the ticket's link to that job.
AC-10 [integration]: The same DELETE with the root token under a wait policy answers 204 with an empty body and writes no ApprovalRequest row.

AC-12 [unit]: When the registered rest:fleet-jobs.cancel command executes input { slug: 'web', projectId: 'p1', id: 'j1' } with ActorPrincipalLoader.forContext() returning principal a1 and permissions.can(principal, 'fleet.job.cancel', { projectId: 'p1' }) resolving { allowed: false }, its run calls jobs.cancel('a1', 'p1', 'j1', false).

AC-13 [unit]: After onModuleInit, registry.get('fleet.job.cancel', 'rest:fleet-jobs.cancel') returns a command with key 'fleet.job.cancel' and skipKeyRecheck true, and registry.get('fleet.ticket-job.unlink', 'rest:ticket-fleet-jobs.unlink') returns a command with key 'fleet.ticket-job.unlink'.
AC-14 [unit]: The rest:ticket-fleet-jobs.unlink command's run for a principal with id a1 calls fleetTickets.unlink('p1', 'WEB-1', 'j1', 'a1') and answers null.
AC-15 [integration]: Approving the keyed agent's pending unlink after root unlinked the same job while it waited settles the request failed.

userStories.title: Gated schedule create, update, enable and disable
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate the four remaining schedule writes and determine any-row authority from the requester at execution.

**Motivation** — 5a to 5c-2 gated 81 routes.

**Approach** — **Any-row schedule authority is the requester's at execution.** `update`, `enable` and `disable` pass `canAdminister` today, computed in the handler. Their commands compute `permissions.can(principal, 'fleet.schedule.update', { projectId })` when they run, as `ScheduleRouteCommands` does for delete.

- `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/schedules` | `fleet.schedule.create` | `rest:project-fleet-schedules.create` | `{ slug, projectId, schedule: parseBody(CreateScheduleDto, …) }` | `schedules.create(principal.id, projectId, schedule)`.
- `PATCH /projects/:slug/fleet/schedules/:id` | `fleet.schedule.update` | `rest:project-fleet-schedules.update` | `{ slug, projectId, id, patch: parseBody(UpdateScheduleDto, …) }` | `schedules.update(principal.id, projectId, id, patch, <can fleet.schedule.update at execution>)`.
- `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/schedules/:id/enable` | `fleet.schedule.update` | `rest:project-fleet-schedules.enable` | `{ slug, projectId, id }` | `schedules.enable(principal.id, projectId, id, <can at execution>)`.
- `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/schedules/:id/disable` | `fleet.schedule.update` | `rest:project-fleet-schedules.disable` | `{ slug, projectId, id }` | `schedules.disable(principal.id, projectId, id, <can at execution>)`.

Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result`. Keep slug in each new project input for lockProjectSlug. SchedulesModule already has the engine and commands since 5b; the controller already has the gate. In ProjectFleetSchedulesController, create/update/enable/disable gain @ApprovalGated and call the route gate. Preserve @Requires, guard order, @HttpCode, @ApiResponse and handler parameters in order. userStories.title: Gated config edit and regenerate
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate config-edit/regenerate requests and separate regenerate's forge preparation from its execution transaction.

**Motivation** — 5a to 5c-2 gated 81 routes.

**Approach** — **The regenerate splits like the drift check.** `ConfigJobsService.prepareRegenerate(actorId, projectId, repoId, body)` (new) reads the repository first (404 `fleet.repos`, as today), then validates the body, then lists its nax files on the forge. The callback it answers re-reads the repository: one changed since the prepare answers `ConflictAppException({}, 'fleet.repos')`, as `prepareDrift` does. The callback then creates the config job. `submitRegenerate` becomes `(await this.prepareRegenerate(…))()`.

**A deferred job create that loses the active-job race fails the request.** `FleetJobsService.dispatch`, `.requeue` and `ConfigJobsService.create` catch `DuplicateActiveJobError`, then look up the winner "outside the failed transaction". Inside the execution transaction, that lookup runs in the aborted transaction, and the request settles `failed`. userStories.title: Ingest writes move to IngestRequeueService and are gated
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Move ingest write orchestration into a reusable service, gate all three global REST writes and defer their background wake until commit.

**Motivation** — 5a to 5c-2 gated 81 routes.

**Approach** — **The ingest writes move to a service.** `FleetIngestController.queue()` holds the write, the activity row, the audit entry and the kick. US-006 moves them, unchanged, into `IngestRequeueService` (`fleet/ingest/ingest-requeue.service.ts`) with `backfill(actorId)`, `rerunJob(actorId, jobId)` and `rerunOutdated(actorId)`. `rerunJob` also takes over the job lookup (404 `fleet.jobs`). The commands call the same methods. The controller keeps only the list route's collaborator (`BUNDLE_INGEST_REPOSITORY`) and gains `ApprovalRouteGate`.

**The ingest kick and the knowledge enqueue use `committedEffect`.** `BundleIngestService.kick()` and `KnowledgeIndexQueue.enqueue(repoId, 'admin')` start background work that reads the rows the route just wrote. Both are in-memory wake signals, like `RunnerNotifier.notify`. Each is wrapped in `committedEffect(() => …)` and called after the write's own `txManager.run` returns. The approval execution wraps its transaction in `withCommittedEffects`, so a deferred write queues the wake until the commit. On the immediate path there is no owning scope, so the wake runs at once, after the write committed, as today.

A deferred-only wake has this shape (the ingest kick; the knowledge enqueue is the same):
```ts
const queued = await this.txManager.run(async () => { /* the write, the activity row, the audit entry, as today */ });
committedEffect(() => this.ingest.kick());
return { queued };
```

Create IngestRouteCommands/INGEST_ROUTE_VARIANTS with these global scope (`projectId: null`) contracts:
- `POST /fleet/ingest/backfill` | `fleet.ingest.backfill` | `rest:fleet-ingest.backfill` | `{}` | `ingestRequeue.backfill(principal.id)`.
- `POST /fleet/ingest/jobs/:jobId/rerun` | `fleet.ingest.rerun` | `rest:fleet-ingest.rerun-job` | `{ jobId }` | `ingestRequeue.rerunJob(principal.id, jobId)`.
- `POST /fleet/ingest/rerun-outdated` | `fleet.ingest.rerun` | `rest:fleet-ingest.rerun-outdated` | `{}` | `ingestRequeue.rerunOutdated(principal.id)`.

Id and string members are read with `parseRouteInput`. Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result`. Preserve the existing repository calls with INGEST_PARSER_VERSION, activity bookkeeping, actorType USER, conditional audit only when queued > 0, result `{ queued }` and list route. Rerun target existence is a command/service check, not a new pre-gate handler check: missing targets may open requests that later fail. IngestModule imports ApprovalEngineModule/AuthRepositoryModule and provides IngestRequeueService/IngestRouteCommands. FleetIngestController constructor becomes `(BUNDLE_INGEST_REPOSITORY, ApprovalRouteGate)`. Three writes gain @ApprovalGated and gate calls, preserving parameters in order, @Requires and existing responses/statuses. Pending throws ApprovalPending; executed returns JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result), 201 as today. Remove these three PENDING_GATE_ROUTES rows.

Each test seeds its own job with a bundle artifact, as fleet-ingest-api.integration.spec.ts does. The activity rows of the ingest and job writes still record `actorType: 'USER'` for an agent actor, as today. **Interface** — `IngestRequeueService` with `backfill(actorId)`, `rerunJob(actorId, jobId)` and `rerunOutdated(actorId)`; `IngestRouteCommands`, `INGEST_ROUTE_VARIANTS` — new: `backfill`, `rerunJob`, `rerunOutdated`. `IBundleIngestRepository.backfill(parserVersion)`, `.rerunJob(jobId)`, `.rerunOutdated(parserVersion)`; `BundleIngestService.kick()`.

**Goal** — Gate corpus-pattern save and repository reindex via a new admin service, preserving kill-switch refusals and commit-safe indexing wakes.

**Motivation** — 5a to 5c-2 gated 81 routes.

**Approach** — **The knowledge writes move to a service.** `ProjectKnowledgeController.patterns` and `.reindex` hold the save, the pass queueing, the audit entry and the enqueue. US-007 moves them into `KnowledgeIndexAdmin` (`fleet/knowledge/knowledge-index-admin.service.ts`) with `savePatterns(projectId, patterns)` and `reindex(projectId, repoId)`. The controller loses `KnowledgeIndexQueue` and `AuditRecorder` and gains `ApprovalRouteGate`. It keeps the kill switch of the reindex (409 before the gate). `KnowledgeIndexAdmin.reindex` checks the kill switch again when it runs and throws `ConflictAppException({}, 'knowledge.disabled')`, so a reindex approved after indexing was switched off settles `failed` instead of recording a pass that `enqueue` silently drops.

**The reindex answers 202 on both paths.** Its executed answer is `202 { queued: true }`, as today. A waiting request answers 202 with the pending summary, as every gated route does. A client tells them apart by the body. OpenAPI holds one response per status, so the handler drops its own `@ApiResponse({ status: 202, type: KnowledgeReindexResultDto })` and documents the executed body in its `@ApiOperation` summary; the documented 202 is `@ApprovalGated()`'s.

**The ingest kick and the knowledge enqueue use `committedEffect`.** `BundleIngestService.kick()` and `KnowledgeIndexQueue.enqueue(repoId, 'admin')` start background work that reads the rows the route just wrote. Both are in-memory wake signals, like `RunnerNotifier.notify`. Each is wrapped in `committedEffect(() => …)` and called after the write's own `txManager.run` returns. The approval execution wraps its transaction in `withCommittedEffects`, so a deferred write queues the wake until the commit. - `POST /projects/:slug/knowledge/repos/:repoId/reindex` | `fleet.knowledge.repo.reindex` | `rest:project-knowledge.reindex` | `{ slug, projectId, repoId }` | `knowledgeAdmin.reindex(projectId, repoId)`.

userStories.title: Gated project fleet decide
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate project fleet ask decisions by type while recording the inner decision in the outer transaction and executing approved inner commands only after commit.

**Motivation** — 5a to 5c-2 gated 81 routes.

**Approach** — The project fleet decide route mirrors 5a's `POST /approvals/:id/decisions` (variant `rest:approvals.decide`). It gates under the type key (`fleet.approval.decide.bash` for a `fleet.job.shell.escalate` ask, `fleet.approval.decide.budget` for a `fleet.budget.override` ask). Its command records the decision. The approved command runs from `afterCommit`, and `skipKeyRecheck` is set.

**The fleet decide gains step methods beside `decide`.** `ApprovalsService.decide` today does: steps 1 to 3, the body translation, `ApprovalDecisionService.decide` (record, then execute), and the reload. It stays exactly as it is, so the global `/fleet/approvals/:id/decide` route and its spec keep their behaviour. Four new methods share its private helpers (`findVisible`, `engineDecision`, `refusalOf`, `decideFailure`):
- `checkDecide(caller, route, id, dto, now)` runs steps 1 to 3 and the translation, and answers `{ key, input }`. `key` is `fleet.approval.decide.bash` when the request's `permissionKey` is `fleet.job.shell.escalate`, else `fleet.approval.decide.budget`. `input` is `{ requestId, decision, comment, params? }`.
- `recordDecide(principal, input)` calls `ApprovalDecisionService.recordDecision(requestId, decision, comment, now, params)`. It reloads the request (`queries.findById`) and builds the decider from `principal`, so it can map errors through `decideFailure(error, request, decider)` as `decide` does.
- `executeDecided(principal, requestId)` calls `ApprovalExecutionService.execute(requestId)` with the same mapping.
- `view(id)` reloads the ask and keeps the `job_ended` 409.

`ApprovalsService` gains `ApprovalExecutionService` (last constructor parameter). The project handler runs `checkDecide`, then gates with `keyCheck: false`: eligibility was checked, and the type keys are metadata the guard does not enforce. On `executed` with `decision === 'approve'`, it runs `executeDecided`, then answers `view(id)`. The commands' `afterCommit` runs `ApprovalExecutionService.execute(requestId)` for an approve, as 5a's does.

Request checks the handler makes today stay before the gate, so they answer as today and open no request: the fleet decide's steps 1 to 3 (visible ask, pending, eligibility) and its body translation (400 `fleet.approvalInput`, 409 `fleet.budgetNotPaused`, …). Every other check runs inside the command, at once or after approval; a failing check settles the request `failed`. This is 5a's rule.

Route contract: `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/approvals/:id/decide` | `fleet.approval.decide.bash` or `.budget` (by the ask) | project, `keyCheck: false` | `rest:project-fleet-approvals.decide` | `{ requestId, decision, comment, params? }` (from `checkDecide`) | `approvals.recordDecide(principal, input)`; `afterCommit`: execute the inner request on approve; `skipKeyRecheck: true`; `toResult: ApprovalRequestSummaryDto.from`. `fleet.approval.decide.bash` and `fleet.approval.decide.budget` each register one command with the same variant and the same spec; they differ only in `key`. Parse ids and translated decision/comment/optional params using the shipped decision command's validation shape. The fleet-decide input is exactly the translated input above, not an additional slug/body envelope.

ApprovalsModule provides FleetApprovalRouteCommands; it imports the engine already and needs AuthRepositoryModule for ActorPrincipalLoader. ProjectFleetApprovalsController gains ApprovalRouteGate last and @ApprovalGated on decide. Keep handler parameters in order, @Requires service-enforced type metadata, guard order, @HttpCode(200) and existing responses. Pending throws ApprovalPending; executed approve invokes executeDecided before returning JsonResponse.Ok(await approvals.view(id)); reject just returns view. Remove the project-decide PENDING_GATE_ROUTES row. Add ApprovalExecutionService as sixth argument to approvals.service.spec.ts's construction; every existing decide assertion still holds (decide still calls decisions.decide); new methods' cases add recordDecision to the decisions double. Controller cases assert checkDecide, gate call and executed mapping.

Each integration test seeds its own pending bash ask through seedFleetAsk with job/runner/lease rows as in fleet-approvals-decide.integration.spec.ts's bashAsk helper. Asks carry approverMustHoldAction true, so the deciding agent holds approval.decide and fleet.job.shell.escalate in P, not necessarily the metadata type key. The agent's pending deny is POST with `{ decision: 'deny' }` under a wait policy for fleet.approval.decide.bash; translation freezes decision reject and comment null. Approving the outer request uses root's global /api/approvals/:id/decisions route. Map inner not-pending/expired errors to fleet.approvalNotPending so a changed inner ask fails the outer request instead of escaping as the outer engine row's concurrency exception.

**Scope** — In: four service methods beside unchanged decide, two type-key registrations for one REST variant, two-phase project handler, module and allowlist.
